results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
Mono green storm is a brew. The green storm cards in Premodern are Hunting Pack and Sprouting Vines. Let me check them and look for a close shell.Hunting Pack is in 31 recent lists. Sprouting Vines has not shown up. Elves is the closest shell. Pulling its numbers.Enough to build. Submitting.Submitted. Premodern, mono green Hunting Pack storm. This is a brew. No mono green storm list exists in the last 30 days of results.

**Shell**
The mana base is the Elves core. Llanowar Elves, Fyndhorn Elves, Priest of Titania, Quirion Ranger, Wirewood Symbiote, Multani's Acolyte, and Gaea's Cradle are all 100% in the 7 Elves lists on record. I cut Survival of the Fittest (also 100%) and the red splash for Anger. A storm deck wants to cast spells, not pitch them.

**How it storms**
- Priest of Titania and Gaea's Cradle make the mana. Quirion Ranger untaps Priest.
- Wirewood Symbiote bounces Multani's Acolyte. Recast it for GG. Each cast is a storm count and a card. Untap Priest in the process.
- Lotus Petal is 4 free storm counts. 160 recent lists play it.
- Land Grant is often free. 2 lists play it. Two more storm counts that also find a Forest.
- Hunting Pack is the kill. 7 mana, one 4/4 Beast per copy. Storm 5 is six 4/4s at instant speed. It appears in 31 recent lists, 1 of them Elves at 2 copies.
- Concordant Crossroads gives the Beasts haste. It has not shown up in results. It is a World Enchantment at G, so the opponent can kill it with a second World Enchantment. Rare in this field.
- Kamahl, Fist of Krosa is the backup kill. 43% of Elves lists run 1. Overrun on a Beast board ends the game.
- Deranged Hermit at 2 pumps Cradle by 5 creatures. 100% in Elves.
- Sylvan Library at 2 keeps the spells flowing. 954 recent lists.

**Sideboard**
Built from the Elves average board. Naturalize 3 (100%), Tormod's Crypt 2 (71%), Winter Orb 2 (57%), Uktabi Orangutan 1 (57%), Xantid Swarm 3 (29%). Xantid Swarm matters more here than in regular Elves. A 7 mana instant into UB Psychatog or Standstill counters needs protection. Wellwisher 2 for Sligh. Caller of the Claw 2 for sweepers and Masticore.

**Known risks**
- Hunting Pack at 7 is heavy. Hands without Priest or Cradle stall.
- Engineered Plague or Masticore wipes the Elves and the storm engine with them.
- Concordant Crossroads is untested. Cut to 1 or swap for a third Wall of Blossoms if you want fewer blanks.

Name a matchup and I will tune the board for it.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
Premodern. GW Replenish, built on the Enchantress shell. Submitted and legal.

**Why this shape**

Stock Replenish is UW. All 37 lists in the window play Island, Attunement, Frantic Search, and Intuition. Cutting blue removes the whole draw and discard engine. The only non-blue Replenish lists in results are a GW variant at 5% (2 of 37 decks), running Brushland, Serra's Sanctum, Enchantress's Presence, Wild Growth, Sterling Grove. That is the version here. The server tags it as Enchantress, the format's top deck at 13.8% share, 65 appearances.

**Main, 60**

- 4 Argothian Enchantress, 4 Enchantress's Presence. Draw engine replacing Attunement and Frantic Search. Both 100% stock in Enchantress.
- 4 Wild Growth. Ramp. Put it on Windswept Heath, crack it, and the aura goes to the yard for Replenish.
- 4 Opalescence, 4 Parallax Wave, 4 Replenish. The kill. Wave fades out, Replenish brings it back under Opalescence, exile their board for good. Stock Replenish runs 3.9 of each.
- 4 Swords to Plowshares. 100% in Replenish, 3.9 copies.
- 3 Seal of Cleansing, 3 Sterling Grove, 2 Aura of Silence. Removal that sacrifices itself, so Replenish rebuys it. All stock in Enchantress.
- 1 Sylvan Library, 1 Exploration. Library is flex at 22%, Exploration stock at 53%.
- 22 lands: 4 Serra's Sanctum, 4 Brushland, 4 Windswept Heath, 5 Forest, 5 Plains.

**What got cut and why**

Decree of Silence is 100% in UW Replenish, but it costs {6}{U}{U}. The first build tripped the color check as Bant. Swapped for the third Sterling Grove and second Aura of Silence.

**Side, 15**

- 3 Exalted Angel. 97% of Replenish boards.
- 4 Defense Grid. 76%. Colorless, so it stays.
- 2 Xantid Swarm. Green replacement for the Hydroblast slot against counterspells. Fringe in Replenish boards at 5%.
- 2 Sphere of Law. 32% flex, for Sligh at 10.6% share.
- 2 Tormod's Crypt. 5% fringe, for Hermit Druid and Psychatog.
- 2 Ray of Revelation. 5% fringe, for the Enchantress mirror.

Meddling Mage and Hydroblast are the other stock board cards. Both need blue, so they are out. Name a matchup and I will score the board against it.

results.text:

I'll preview both and grab a real Merfolk list.Every candidate scored a hit against both decks. Now the submission.Deck submitted. Modern Merfolk, stock main, sideboard tuned for the top two decks.

**The field**
Broodscale Combo is 17.3% of the field. Prowess is 9.3%. Nothing else is above 6.1%. The build targets those two.

**Main 60**
This is the fart_sniffer_93 League 5-0 list from October 12 and 13, unchanged. Every card is stock in the 6 Merfolk results from the window. Harbinger of the Seas 100%, Tide Shaper 83%, Aether Vial 83%, Flare of Denial 83%, Sink into Stupor 83%, Cavern of Souls 83%.

Why the main already matters against the top decks:
- Harbinger of the Seas. Broodscale runs 16.7 nonbasics: 4 Eldrazi Temple, 4 Urza's Saga, 3.2 Ugin's Labyrinth. Harbinger turns all of them into Islands. No Temple mana, no Saga constructs. Prowess runs 15.3 nonbasics, 3.3 Steam Vents and 10 fetches. Harbinger shuts off their red.
- Tide Shaper. Kicked, it Islands one Eldrazi Temple or Steam Vents. Gets +1/+1 while they control an Island, which Harbinger guarantees.
- Flare of Denial and Sink into Stupor. Counter and bounce for the Broodscale plus Blade combo. Flare pitches a Merfolk.

**Sideboard 15**
- 4 Chalice of the Void (100% of Merfolk boards). Set to 1 against Prowess: Dragon's Rage Channeler, Monastery Swiftspear, and their burn spells. Set to 1 against Broodscale: Basking Broodscale costs 2 but the Blade, Haywire Mite, and Saga targets are 1 or less.
- 4 Consign to Memory (83% of Merfolk boards). Counters colorless spells and triggered abilities. Broodscale's combo is a chain of colorless triggers and Eldrazi casts. Emrakul, the Promised End at 3.9 copies is colorless.
- 4 Force of Negation (67% of Merfolk boards). Free counter on their turn. Hits Broodscale noncreature combo pieces and Prowess burn.
- 3 Stern Scolding. Counters creature spells with power or toughness 2 or less for one mana. Prowess creatures are all 1/1 and 1/2. Basking Broodscale is a 2/2 and Haywire Mite is 1/1. Stern Scolding sits at 17% adoption in Merfolk mains, 1 list at 4 copies. I put it over Mystical Dispute because neither top deck is blue, so Dispute costs 3 against them.

**What I cut from the stock board**
Mystical Dispute (33%) and Subtlety (reference list). Dispute is full price against non-blue decks. Subtlety is fine but costs 3 or a blue card. Stern Scolding answers the same bodies for one mana.

**Sideboarding guide**
- vs Broodscale: in 4 Consign, 4 Force, 2 Chalice. Out 4 Snapback, 4 Silvergill Adept, 2 Mutavault.
- vs Prowess: in 4 Chalice, 3 Stern Scolding. Out 4 Flare of Denial, 3 Harbinger of the Seas. Chalice on 1 is the main plan, so keep Vial to cast around it.

Want me to tune this for a third matchup, like Devoted Druid Combo or Affinity?

No mono white control put up results in the last 30 days. The shell is UW Control (2.2% share, 44 league trophies) with the blue stripped out, plus white tools from Boros Land Destruction.

**The core, from UW Control (84 decks)**
- 4 Solitude: 100% adoption. Free removal and a Kaheera legal Elemental.
- 4 Orim's Chant, 3 Silence, 2 Isochron Scepter: 96%, 89%, 90%. Scepter on Chant is the fun part. Scepter on Silence is the backup.
- 2 Wrath of the Skies: 99%. Hits creatures and artifacts, which matters against Broodscale Combo (17.3% share) and Affinity (5.5%).
- 1 March of Otherworldly Light: 81%. Second copy added since Prismatic Ending is bad in one color.
- Monumental Henge and Geier Reach Sanitarium: 96% each. Henge digs for Scepter, Beza, Elspeth, and Emperor.

**From Boros Land Destruction (60 decks)**
- 4 Path to Exile: 100%.
- 3 Field of Ruin: 100% there. Three copies, not four, because Elspeth and Wrath need WW.
- 2 Wrath of God: 17% flex. Replaces Supreme Verdict.
- 1 Castle Ardenvale: 68%.
- 2 Mana Tithe: 5% fringe. Cheap, and it pitches to nothing but it is funny on turn two.

**Added for mono white**
- 3 The Wandering Emperor: 143 Modern lists this window. Flash removal and tokens.
- 2 Elspeth, Sun's Champion: has not shown up in results. Your top end and a one card win.
- 2 Beza, the Bounding Spring: 226 lists. Elemental, so Kaheera stays legal.
- 2 Sunset Revelry, 1 Timely Reinforcements: 4 and 3 lists. Life and bodies against Prowess (9.3% share).
- 1 Eiganjo, Seat of the Empire: free spell in a land slot.

**Sideboard**
Built from the UW Control average board where the cards are white. 3 High Noon (95% there), 1 Kaheera (89%), 1 Surgical Extraction (82%). Mystical Dispute and Consign to Memory are gone, so the slots went to 2 Rest in Peace and 2 Relic of Progenitus for Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, and Storm, plus 2 more Wrath of God, 2 Timely Reinforcements, and 2 Mana Tithe.

**What you lose**
No Teferi, no Narset, no Day's Undoing, no counterspells past Tithe. Card draw is thin. Henge, Beza, and Sanitarium carry that.

**What the usual list is**

Greasefang is a Tier C deck in the 30-day window, 10 appearances, 27 league trophies. The stock build is Orzhov: Monument to Endurance, Fleeting Spirit, Iron-Shield Elf, Guardian of New Benalia, and The Mycosynth Gardens all sit at 81% adoption. Parhelion II and Thoughtseize are 100%. This list drops the whole Monument package and goes green for a self-mill engine.

**What is different**

- Satyr Wayfinder (4): mills 4, finds a land. 0 recent Pioneer results. The core of the brew.
- Can't Stay Away (2): reanimates Greasefang from the yard, with flashback. 0 recent results.
- Grisly Salvage (4): dig 5, keep a creature or land. 3 decks in the format.

**Risks**

The stock list's Monument and Fleeting Spirit give it a non-combo plan. This list is more all-in on the yard. Soul-Guide Lantern and Rest in Peace effects hurt more here. Name a matchup and I will score the board against it.

results.prompt: Combine Living End and Scam into one Modern deck.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the current field for both archetypes.Deck submitted and validated. Modern, four-color Living End Scam. This is a brew.

**Why the classic Scam cards are out**

- Grief and Fury: illegal in Modern.
- Not Dead After All, Undying Malice, Feign Death, Ephemerate: all mana value 1. Violent Outburst and Shardless Agent cascade into the first nonland card under 3. Any of those would be hit instead of Living End. Living End lists run zero nonland cards below 3 for this reason.

**The Scam package, mana value 3**

- 2 Minion's Return. Flash aura. Evoke Subtlety or Endurance, respond to the sacrifice trigger, enchant it. It dies and comes straight back untapped. Turn 3 you get a 3/3 flyer or a 3/4 reach for three mana and no card disadvantage. If it is still on board when Living End resolves, it dies and returns again. 0 recent Modern results.
- 2 Ghostly Flicker. Evoke two Incarnations, flicker both in response. Neither gets sacrificed. Also resets Endurance to shuffle your own graveyard away under Endurance from the other side, or blinks a Misty Rainforest to refetch. 1 recent Modern result.

Neither card has appeared alongside Living End in the 30-day window.

**Base: Mighty_Ravendark, Modern League 5-0, 2026-10-13**

Cuts to fit the four slots: Brazen Borrower (18% adoption), Vibrance, one Waker of Waves (59%, 1.7 avg copies), Flare of Denial (18%), Otawara. Everything else is stock: Endurance, Subtlety, Wistfulness, Force of Negation, Living End all at 100% of 80 lists. Violent Outburst 85%. Street Wraith 85%. Oliphaunt 86%.

**Mana**

Black comes from Watery Grave and Undercity Sewers, both already in 14% of Living End lists, fetched by 4 Misty Rainforest. Six black sources for a two-of. Otawara and Boseiju were cut to make room. Red stays for Outburst and Oliphaunt through Steam Vents, Stomping Ground, Commercial District, Thundering Falls.

**Sideboard**

Average Living End board runs 4 Clarion Conqueror at 70%, but that needs white and this list has none. Swapped for black and colorless answers that appeared in the niuwaid001 and Mighty_Ravendark boards. Mystical Dispute 4 (100% adoption), Brotherhood's End 2 (64%), Force of Vigor 2 (93%), Inevitable Betrayal 2 (78%), Faerie Macabre 2, Foundation Breaker 1, Dismember 1, Damping Sphere 1.

**Honest read**

Ghostly Flicker costs three mana where Ephemerate cost one. The Scam turn here is turn 3, not turn 1. The upside is that the same cards still cascade cleanly and still get reanimated by Living End. If you want the turn 1 version, it does not exist in Modern without breaking cascade.

**How it wins**
- Dream Halls resolves. Discard any blue card to cast Morphling. Discard a blue card to cast Opportunity or Rush of Knowledge to refill. Morphling is blue, so every cantrip and draw spell in hand pays for it. Rush of Knowledge off Morphling draws 5.
- Show and Tell puts Akroma or Dream Halls into play directly. Akroma has haste, so Show and Tell on turn 2 off Ancient Tomb plus Petal is a 6-point clock immediately.
- Intuition for three Morphling leaves one in hand. Intuition for three Dream Halls does the same.
- Orim's Chant protects the turn you go off.

**What changed from the stock shell**
- Cut: 1 Brain Freeze, 1 Circular Logic, 3 Cunning Wish, 1 Opt. Brain Freeze was 100% adoption. Cunning Wish was 60%. Without a storm kill, Wish loses its main target.
- Added: 3 Morphling, 2 Akroma. Both are legal. Morphling shows up in 84 recent lists format-wide. Akroma shows up in 210. Neither appears in any Dream Halls result.
- Everything else matches the archetype: Dream Halls, Meditate, Opportunity, Rush of Knowledge, Intuition, Show and Tell, Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors, Svyelunite Temple all at 100% adoption. Lotus Petal, Orim's Chant, Adarkar Wastes at 60%.

Defense Grid 3 (60% adoption), Blue Elemental Blast 2 (100%), Chain of Vapor 2 (100%), Teferi's Response 2 (60%), Abeyance, Rushing River, Stifle, Tolarian Winds 1 each (60%). The two open slots went to Hydroblast, which bparis15 ran in Challenge 16. Sligh is 10.6% of the field, so four Blast effects is reasonable.

**Weak points to know**
- Akroma can only be cast off Dream Halls by discarding a white card. Only 5 white cards in the deck. Treat Akroma as a Show and Tell card, not a Dream Halls card.
- Morphling needs mana to protect itself. Save Petals or an untapped Island after you go off if the opponent has Swords to Plowshares.
